questions: Q1: Does the CLI build succeed with the new netsuite and run handler files?
Q2: Does the CLI help text correctly show both new commands?
Q3: Does the manifest default env reading work correctly for both handlers?

answers.answer: Yes. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits with code 0 and `npm run build` succeeds. Both new files (src/inspect/netsuite.ts and src/run/index.ts) compile correctly with proper imports from existing lib modules.
evidence: npx tsc --noEmit exit code 0 in helix-cli directory
npm run build exit code 0 producing dist/ output
Both files use existing imports: HxConfig, hxFetch, resolveRepo, getFlag, getPositionalArgs

answers.answer: Yes. `node dist/index.js --help` shows `hlx run` and `hlx inspect netsuite` in the top-level help. `node dist/index.js inspect --help` shows the netsuite subcommand usage. Both help texts match the implementation plan specification.
evidence: Top-level help output includes 'hlx run --repo <name> <code>' and 'hlx inspect netsuite --repo <name> --query "<suiteql>"'
Inspect help output includes netsuite with query and logs modes

answers.answer: Yes. Both handlers (cmdNetsuite and cmdRun) share the same readManifestDefaultEnv pattern: read /tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json, check nsDefaultEnv field, map PRODUCTION→prod and SANDBOX→sandbox. The --env flag overrides the manifest default when provided.

statement: Implementation complete for helix-cli. All 5 steps executed: netsuite handler (cmdNetsuite with query/logs modes), run handler (cmdRun with code/modules/env), inspect router integration (case 'netsuite'), main dispatcher integration (case 'run'), and quality gates (typecheck pass, build pass, help text verified). Both handlers follow existing patterns from db.ts and logs.ts, use hxFetch for server communication, and read nsDefaultEnv from the inspection manifest.
